description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
6.0 adds word indexing and more control over ranking, and it is faster. The fault tolerance
      and pattern matching Indx is known for are still there.
      
      - **Word indexing.** A field's words are indexed as words. A query word is looked up as typed,
        then within one, two or three edits, and exact matches come first.
      - **Ranking control.** How records are fetched and whether they are reranked are separate
        choices, and each field has its own typo tolerance and its own weight in the ordering.
      - **Speed.** Searching and loading are faster and use less memory.
      - **Pattern matching.** Matching inside words, with its tolerance for heavily misspelt text, is
        chosen field by field: on its own, or together with word matching.
      
      Most code written for 5.0 needs changes before it builds, and result lists change by design. The
      [v5 to v6 migration guide](https://github.com/indxSearch/skill-indx-search/blob/v6/references/migration-v5-to-v6.md)
      says where each 5.0 setting went. The fixes of 5.0.6 are included.
      
      ### Performance
      
      6.0 is faster and more optimized than 5.0. Searches take less time and allocate less memory,
      most of all on datasets with many searched fields or long texts. Loading is faster and takes less
      memory. Facets over large result sets, a filter on one of many values and combined filters are
      faster too, and a search after deletes and a reindex is as fast as on a fresh engine.
      
      ### Main changes
      
      - **Typo tolerance by levels.** A record holding the words as typed is never placed below one
        holding a misspelling. `Result.CountedTolerance` says which level the hits are on and
        `Result.ToleranceCounts` how many there are on each. `Tolerance.ThreeEdits` is new, for long
        words.
      - **One set of records for count, facets and list.** `Result.Count` is the number of records that
        answer the search. Facets are counted over all of them, not the returned rows, and a facet's
        number is the number a filter on that value returns. `Fiction` and `FICTION` are one value.
      - **Search as you type.** A search answers from the first letter. The word being typed also finds
        the longer words it starts, from two letters by default (`Match.TypingPrefixFrom`); a finished
        word is matched whole.
      - **When no record holds every word.** The list is the records holding most of the words, marked
        `Result.IsFallback`, or empty (`Candidates.Fallback`). A short page can be filled from the next
        typo level (`Candidates.FillReach`), and partial matches can follow the hits (`Candidates.Rest`).
      - **Compound words.** A word finds the compounds it ends ("ost" finds "brunost"), a compound finds
        the records holding its parts, and words written together or apart find each other. It works
        from the words in the index, with no dictionary and no language setting.
      - **Synonyms.** A synonym is an alternative to the words typed, so it widens a search: "war film",
        with film and movie as synonyms, also finds the war movies. Records holding the typed words come
        first.
      - **Reranking.** What 5.0 called Coverage is now the reranker: it orders the fetched records by
        how well they cover the query. It is on by default and switched with `Ranking.Rerank`, apart
        from how the records are fetched (`Query.Mode`). `Result.Reranked` says whether it ran.
      - **Matching per field.** A field is matched by its words (`Field.WordMatching`), inside its
        words (`Field.PatternMatching`), or both, with its own typo tolerance (`Field.Tolerance`) and
        its own weight in the ordering (`Field.RerankWeight`).
      - **Codes and numbers.** A field can have text rules of its own (`FieldProxy.TextRules`), and a
        rule can keep the original (`TextRule.KeepOriginal`): an ISBN is found with hyphens, without
        them, or in part. A search for a number no record holds can return nothing
        (`Candidates.NoFallbackForNumbersFrom`).
      - **Filter expressions.** `CreateFilter` takes an expression such as
        `brand IN ["nike", "puma"] AND price BETWEEN 100 AND 2000 AND NOT category = "outlet"`, and
        `Filter.ToExpression()` writes any filter back as one. New filters: one of a set of values
        (`CreateInFilter`), within a distance of a position (`CreatePositionFilter`), dates
        (`CreateDateFilter`, `CreateDateRangeFilter`) and custom (`CreateCustomFilter<T>`).
      - **Bury.** `CreateBury` lowers the records a filter holds and moves nothing else, where a boost
        lowers every record it does not lift.
      - **Vector search.** The search graph is new: recall is higher, it builds faster, and a document
        with a vector takes less memory. A filtered vector search returns as many as were asked for. The graphs can be saved and loaded (`SaveEmbeddings`, `LoadEmbeddings`).
      - **Match report.** With `Query.EnableMatchReport`, each returned record says how every query
        word was met and in which field.
      - **Query fit.** With `Query.MeasureFit`, a search also says how much of the text its best
        results explain, which separates a search from a question.
      - **Backup.** A store can be copied while in use (`SqLiteBackup.Take`); the copy is verified.
      
      ### Upgrading from 5.0
      
      The guide has the details; these are the changes that stop a build or change a list.
      
      - **The query in three parts.** Every setting of a search lives on `Query.Match` (what counts as
        a hit), `Query.Candidates` (which records come in) or `Query.Ranking` (the order).
        `CoverageSetup`, `WordLookupSetup`, `FieldCoverage`, `Query.CoverageDepth`, `EnableCoverage`,
        `EnableBoost` and every truncation setting are gone.
      - **Fetching and reranking are two choices.** `Query.Mode` is how records are fetched
        (`SearchMode.EditDistance`, the default, or `SearchMode.Bm25f`) and `Ranking.Rerank` whether
        they are reranked. For 5.0's `EnableCoverage = false`, write `Mode = SearchMode.Bm25f` with
        `Ranking.Rerank = false`.
      - **`Field.Searchable` is gone.** Set `WordMatching`, `PatternMatching` or both. A field
        configuration fresh from `Init` searches nothing until one of them is set; `WordMatching = true`
        with `PatternMatching = PatternMatchingSetup.Default` is the nearest to 5.0. A saved
        configuration is read as it was searched.
      - **Renamed.** `Field.CoverageStrictness` is `Field.Tolerance` (`Exact`, `OneEdit`, `TwoEdits`),
        `Field.CoverageWeight` is `Field.RerankWeight`, `Query.EnableCoverageReport` is
        `EnableMatchReport`, and `WordTrieSetup` is `CompoundSetup`.
      - **Pattern settings are the field's.** The index sizes and the start and stop characters moved
        from `IndexerSetup` to each field's `PatternMatchingSetup`; `IndexerSetup.Dense` and `SingleWord`
        are gone. High resolution is gone: words typed together or apart are matched by
        `Match.JoinedWords`, on by default.
      - **The scoring mode is chosen.** `ScoringSetup` in `ConfigurationParameters` chooses
        `ScoringMode.BM25F`, the default, or `ScoringMode.BM25PerField`. `Field.BM25k1` is read only in
        the per-field mode, so a dataset whose fields had different values ranks differently unless it
        is built with `BM25PerField`.
      - **Words.** The shortest word is two letters in every field (`TokenizerSetup.MinimumWordSize`),
        and a word may be 100 characters long (`MaxSizeOfWordToken`), so long compounds are words.
      - **Field settings.** `TrySetFieldConfiguration` returns every refusal with its reason and no
        longer throws for some; `TryValidateFieldConfiguration` asks without changing anything.
        `Field.CaseSensitive` and `Field.TextNormalizer` can be set at any time and take effect at the
        next `Load`; `TrySetCaseSensitive` and `TrySetTextNormalizer` are gone.
      - **Filters and boosts.** `CreateBoost` returns `Boost?` and refuses a null filter. The
        `CreateRangeFilter` overload taking a culture is gone, with `RangeFilter.Culture`.
      - **Vectors.** A vector field has no other role, a vector of the wrong length is refused, and
        vectors are compared by cosine whatever their length. Scores and order of vector and hybrid
        results change. The `HNSW` and `MessagePack` packages are no longer dependencies.
      - **Over HTTP (`Indx.Http`).** `QueryProxy` takes `mode`, `match`, `candidates` and `ranking`,
        every setting optional: one left out is the dataset's on an Indx server, then the default. The
        result has `count`, `ranked`, `isFallback`, `toleranceCounts` and `countedTolerance`. Enums are
        written by name.
      - **Lifecycle.** A `Load` that fails leaves no documents and the state `Error`, and `Status` says
        `Ready` only when `Index()` has finished everything.
      
      ### Also new
      
      - `Result.Ranked` (how many records were ranked), `Result.Reranked` and `Result.Fill` (how many
        listed records came from a fill).
      - `Candidates.IndexTerms`: score with the query's whole words, its pieces, or both.
      - `Filter.And(params Filter[])` and `Filter.Or(params Filter[])`: one filter over any number.
      - `FilterKeyReader.Operands(key)`: what a filter key holds, read without an engine.
      - `EmbeddingSetup` in `ConfigurationParameters`: how vectors are held in memory, and when a graph
        rebuilds itself. `IEmbeddingIndex.TryGetVector` reads a document's vector back.
      - A reason for the last `false`s that had none: `DeleteJsonRecord`, `DeleteJsonRecords` and
        `DeleteFilter` have an overload with `out string error`.
      
      ### Fixed
      
      - A filter built while an insert or update ran could miss the new documents.
      - A search whose filter could not be loaded threw; it now returns the reason on `Result.Reason`.
      - A role or weight set straight on a `Field` is saved, and a role set while a search ran is seen.
      - Documents with one and the same vector no longer hide each other in a vector search.
      - A record whose words are in different fields is found also when one of those fields has a case
        sensitivity or text rules of its own.
      
      ### Known issues in this beta
      
      - **An insert after `Unload()` replaces the stored records.** With a store attached, calling
        `InsertJsonRecords` on an engine that has been unloaded and not loaded again loads the inserted
        records as the whole dataset, in the index and in the store. Load the engine before inserting.
        An Indx server refuses such an insert.
